text:
PENERBITAN Surat Keputusan (SK) Pengangkatan Abdullah sebagai Inspektur Pembantu (Irban) di lingkungan Inspektorat Aceh setelah sekitar dua bulan menjabat mendapat sorotan dari Zulkifli, pengamat hukum di Aceh. Dalam keterangannya kepada AJNN pada 21 September 2026 lalu, Zulkifli ingin kembali memastikan apakah Abdullah telah memenuhi persyaratan jabatan yang berlaku ketika dia diangkat sebagai Irban pada 14 September 2026.

Sorotan dari Zulkifli inilah yang belakangan diduga mendapat perhatian pembaca AJNN dalam sepekan terakhir, sehingga berita "Pengamat Hukum: Dugaan Pemalsuan Pengangkatan Abdullah Jadi Irban Bisa Terancam Pidana" menempati urutan teratas.

Dalam keterangannya, Zulkifli turut menyoroti surat bernomor PEG.821.29/071/2018 yang ditandatangani pada 27 November 2018. Dalam diktum “Memperhatikan” tercantum Surat Menteri Dalam Negeri RI Nomor 800/2372/IJ tertanggal 22 November 2018. Sementara pengangkatan Abdullah sebagai Irban tercatat berlangsung pada 14 September 2018.

Menurut Zulkifli, perbedaan kronologi tersebut perlu diklarifikasi, termasuk memastikan keaslian, dasar penerbitan dan kedudukan surat tersebut dalam proses pengangkatan Abdullah.

Baca Juga

Jalan Terjal Andriy Anta Kacaribu Raih Gelar Doktor di Usia 26 Tahun

Selain ihwal pengangkatan Abdullah sebagai Irban yang diduga abnormal tersebut, informasi tentang mutasi sejumlah perwira Polda Aceh juga diduga turut memantik rasa ingin tahu pembaca AJNN dalam pekan ini. Diketahui, Kapolda Aceh Irjen Pol Ruddi Setiawan kembali melakukan mutasi dan rotasi sejumlah personel melalui Surat Telegram Kapolda Aceh Nomor ST/276/IX/KEP.3./2026 dan ST/276/IX/KEP.3./2026.

Dalam ST tersebut, setidaknya ada 10 personel mengalami pergeseran, rotasi internal maupun pengangkatan jabatan di lingkungan Ditreskrimum Polda Aceh. (Baca selengkapnya: Kapolda Aceh Rombak Jajaran Reserse, Sejumlah Pejabat Ditreskrimum-Ditreskrimsus Bergeser)

Baca Juga

Getar Desak APH Usut Tuntas Administrasi Pengangkatan Irban Inspektorat Aceh

Berita lain yang turut mendapat perhatian pembaca AJNN adalah pelantikan "kabinet" baru di jajaran Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Ar Ranirry Banda Aceh. Pada Jumat, 25 September 2026 lalu, Rektor UIN Ar-Raniry Banda Aceh, Prof. Mujiburrahman, melantik 14 ketua program studi dan 14 sekretaris program studi, disertai satu kepala laboratorium serta penetapan dua dosen sebagai guru besar dan lektor kepala pada Fakultas Tarbiyah dan Keguruan.

Informasi itu telah dipublikasi AJNN dalam berita berjudul "Rektor UIN Ar-Raniry Lantik 14 Pejabat Baru, Ini Daftar Namanya".

Baca Juga

POPULER PEKAN INI:Dari Isu JKA hingga Rusuh Mahasiswa

Ada hal menarik yang disampaikan Prof Mujibburahman dalam pelantikan tersebut, yaitu meminta para pejabat yang dilantik menjalankan amanah dengan memberikan pelayanan terbaik, terukur dan sesuai standar kepada mahasiswa maupun dosen.

“Bekerjalah untuk lembaga, jangan bekerja untuk dekan atau rektor. Berikan pelayanan kepada mahasiswa dan dosen yang terbaik, standar dan sesuai prosedur universitas,” kata Mujiburrahman.

Ia juga meminta setiap persoalan yang muncul di tingkat program studi diselesaikan melalui koordinasi dengan dekan atau wakil dekan sesuai prosedur yang berlaku.

Menurutnya, persoalan antara dosen dan mahasiswa juga harus dimediasi secara serius agar mahasiswa tidak menjadi korban dan dapat menyelesaikan studinya tepat waktu.

“Jika ada masalah antara dosen dan mahasiswa, maka harus terpantau dengan betul-betul serius, jangan sampai mahasiswa menjadi korban, agar mahasiswa dapat menyelesaikan kuliah tepat waktu,” ujarnya.

Di sisi lain, pencapaian Andriy Anta Kacaribu di dunia akademik pun menempati urutan teratas berita yang paling banyak dibaca di AJNN pekan keempat September 2026 ini. Hal ini bukan tanpa alasan lantaran Andriy mampu menyelesaikan program doktor ilmu pertanian Universitas Syiah Kuala (USK) melalui Program Percepatan Doktor (PRUUPD) di usia 26 tahun.

Perjalanan akademik Andriy berlangsung sangat cepat dan konsisten. Ia menyelesaikan pendidikan S1 kimia di FMIPA USK dengan IPK 3,67. Pendidikan itu dia tempuh hanya dalam waktu sekitar 3,5 tahun. dan mendapat Beasiswa Bidikmisi. Selanjutnya, ia menempuh S2 Teknologi Industri Pertanian USK, meraih IPK 4,00 dalam sekitar 1,4 tahun, serta memperoleh Beasiswa Program Riset Unggulan USK. Pada 2023, ia melanjutkan ke jenjang doktor melalui PRUUPD.

Produktivitas riset menjadi bagian penting dari perjalanan tersebut. Andriy telah menghasilkan lebih dari 20 artikel ilmiah pada jurnal internasional bereputasi Q1, Q2, dan Q3, dengan H-index Scopus 6. Selama penyusunan disertasi, ia juga menghasilkan 10 artikel jurnal internasional bereputasi tinggi, dengan tema penelitian meliputi limbah pertanian, POME, sustainable aviation fuel, dan material karbon berbasis biomassa.

Namun, di balik deretan prestasi tersebut terdapat perjuangan yang tidak ringan. Sebagai anak bungsu dari empat bersaudara, Andriy tumbuh di Subulussalam setelah orang tuanya berpisah ketika ia berusia delapan tahun dan ayahnya meninggal dua tahun kemudian. Saat SMP Negeri 3 Sultan Daulat, ia terbiasa berjalan kaki lebih dari 10 kilometer setiap hari untuk pergi-pulang sekolah dan berjualan makanan ringan untuk membantu kebutuhan hidup.

Keterbatasan tidak menghentikan langkahnya. Sejak SD hingga SMA, ia konsisten meraih peringkat pertama di kelas. Setelah lulus SMA pada 2018, ia diterima di USK melalui jalur SNMPTN dengan dukungan Beasiswa Bidikmisi. Dari perjalanan tersebut, langkahnya kemudian berkembang dari ruang kelas menuju laboratorium, publikasi internasional, hingga ruang sidang doktor.

Kisah Andriy menunjukkan bahwa keterbatasan bukan selalu akhir dari sebuah perjalanan. Dengan ketekunan, kesempatan pendidikan, dan kerja keras, jalan yang panjang sekalipun dapat membawa seseorang menuju pencapaian yang jauh lebih besar.

Perjuangan inilah yang diduga mampu menjadi motivasi bagi pembaca AJNN, hingga berita ini masuk dalam daftar trending topik dalam pekan ini.

Terakhir terkait rekaman CCTV nasabah Bank Aceh Syariah yang diduga bocor juga masuk dalam daftar lima besar berita paling banyak dibaca di AJNN. Kali ini, berita tersebut menginformasikan tentang langkah Kantor Hukum ARZ & Rekan mengadukan PT Bank Aceh Syariah (BAS) ke Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) dan Bank Indonesia (BI) terkait dugaan pelanggaran perlindungan konsumen dan pelindungan data pribadi.

Pengaduan kepada OJK tersebut terdaftar dengan Nomor 0028/ARZ/IX/2026 tentang Pengaduan Dugaan Pelanggaran Perlindungan Konsumen atas Kebocoran Data Pribadi oleh PT Bank Aceh Syariah. Sementara pengaduan kepada Bank Indonesia melalui Kepala Perwakilan Bank Indonesia Provinsi Aceh terdaftar dengan Nomor 0029/ARZ/IX/2026 dengan perihal yang sama.

Dalam dokumen pengaduan disebutkan, Malahayati merupakan salah satu nasabah PT Bank Aceh Syariah yang mengalami dugaan tindak pidana penganiayaan pada Selasa, 8 September 2026 sekitar pukul 19.50 WIB.

Kuasa hukum korban, Zulkifli dari Kantor Hukum ARZ & Rekan mengatakan, peristiwa tersebut terjadi di kawasan ATM Bank Aceh, Jalan Diponegoro Nomor 20, Sabang, kawasan Warung Seafood Sabang Merauke dan Anjungan Tunai Mandiri Bank Aceh Syariah di depan Kantor Wali Kota Sabang.

Peristiwa itu kemudian dilaporkan ke Polda Aceh pada 10 September 2026 dengan Nomor Laporan STTLP/B/269/IX/2026/SPKT/Polda Aceh. Dalam laporan tersebut, terlapor disebut atas nama Nazaruddin alias Tgk. Agam, yang dalam laporan polisi disebut sebagai Anggota Dewan Perwakilan Rakyat Aceh dan mantan Wali Kota Sabang.

Ia mengatakan rekaman itu disebut menampilkan identitas dan peristiwa yang menimpa klien, yang seharusnya dilindungi sebagai data pribadi dan tidak disebarluaskan tanpa dasar hukum yang sah.

Sementara PT Bank Aceh Syariah yang menjadi objek pemberitaan memiliki alasan tersendiri menyikapi laporan tersebut. Menurut Pemimpin Divisi Sekretariat Perusahaan Bank Aceh, Ilham Novrizal, bank tidak pernah menyebarluaskan rekaman CCTV tersebut kepada media massa, media sosial maupun kanal publik lainnya. Rekaman CCTV dimaksud diberikan kepada pemohon berdasarkan adanya permohonan tertulis dan identitas pemohon.***

text:
Date

(MENAFN- Bangladesh Monitor) Dhaka: DHL Express and Singapore Airlines (SIA) have renewed their crew and maintenance agreement covering five Boeing 777 freighters based at Singapore Changi Airport, according to a joint release the companies issued recently.

Under the renewed deal, SIA pilots will continue operating the 777s, while SIA engineers will handle their maintenance. The freighters support DHL's intercontinental air network, linking its South Asia Hub in Singapore with key destinations across the United States.

Travis Cobb, Executive Vice President for Network Operations and Aviation at DHL Express, said the renewal underscores the company's commitment to network capacity that keeps global trade moving, calling the five freighters integral to its intercontinental operations and citing Singapore's strength as a logistics hub alongside SIA's operational expertise.

Lee Lik Hsin, Chief Commercial Officer of Singapore Airlines, said the agreement reflects the strength of a partnership that has supported express air freight movement between Asia-Pacific and global markets via Singapore since 2022, combining SIA's expertise with DHL's logistics network to reinforce Singapore's role as a leading air freight hub, particularly in the e-commerce segment.

The five Boeing 777 freighters, which entered service progressively starting in 2022, provide the reliable air capacity required to support time-sensitive, cross-border trade, the release said, adding that each aircraft can carry up to 102 tonnes of cargo and ranks among the world's largest, longest-range, and most capable twin-engine freighters.

With Singapore serving as the home base for the dual-liveried freighters, the renewed partnership deepens DHL's global aviation capabilities while anchoring additional long-haul cargo capacity at Changi Airport.

The agreement underscores both companies' confidence in the sustained growth of international trade and the essential role reliable air connectivity plays in supporting global supply chains.

text:
Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez arrived in New York this week for the UN General Assembly seeking business deals on debt, energy and ​mining, to demonstrate the once sanctioned country was open for business again after US forces removed her predecessor in January.

She pledged in her speech before the UN that the South ‌American OPEC member would hold elections as part of a transition to “full democracy.”

She left with photographs of herself alongside US President Donald Trump, but obtained no concrete agreements.

It was her first visit to the US since American forces captured then-President Nicolas Maduro in a January raid.

It demonstrated Washington’s deep control over her administration and showed Venezuela’s need for new alliances to align with Trump’s aspirations, analysts said.”Rodriguez enjoyed a week of high visibility.

Yet, when we make a list of concrete results, ​the outcome is modest.

Where are the disbursements, the reconstruction package or the business deals?

They did not materialise on the scale that would have allowed New York to be portrayed ​as Venezuela’s great financial comeback,” said Washington-based analyst Antonio De La Cruz.

“To the victor belong the spoils,” Trump said in a Tuesday address to the assembly ⁠as Rodriguez listened, reminding her that the US stood ready to use its “unmatched military might.

“Trump did not mention Rodriguez by name in his speech, and no readout was published on his brief “pull-aside” meeting with her. ​

Leftist leaders from other nations who once backed Maduro kept their distance, while Venezuelans living in the US protested outside the UN with signs depicting Rodriguez in a jail-style orange jumpsuit.

De La Cruz said Trump showed ​Washington is shaping the new Venezuelan landscape, while Rodriguez demonstrated she is the key interlocutor.

“But she now bears an additional consequence: she will have to explain when Venezuelans will actually vote.

“For nine months, Rodriguez had avoided giving signals about an election, while US officials kept expectations at bay by saying it would take time to materialise.

Analysts and Venezuelan opposition parties now say the clock is ticking to set a date, while experts estimate it will take at least 12 months ​to appoint reliable authorities and organise the voting.

text:
By Mohamed Attia

Advisor to the Chairman of the Egyptian Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) and Director General of International Agreements, Karim Gamil, stressed the importance of having regulatory authorities rely on the findings of technical and economic feasibility studies and market indicators when developing and implementing Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) policies.

He said the transition to regulatory requirements should be based on realistic and practical foundations, allowing the aviation sector to achieve its transition goals without placing obligations on countries or industry stakeholders that cannot be realistically implemented.

Speaking as Egypt’s representative at the 9th Forum of the European Civil Aviation Conference (ECAC) in Paris, Capt. Gamil stressed that clear policies and stable regulatory frameworks are key to attracting the investments needed to establish and develop SAF production projects.

Gamil also presented two projects currently under development in Egypt in the field of sustainable bio-based aviation fuel. He highlighted the opportunities these projects offer to strengthen national capabilities in the sector, attract investment, and bring in the technology needed to support the sustainable aviation fuel industry.

Gamil also took part in a high-level panel discussion on the implementation and future of SAF policies, alongside representatives from the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), Brazil’s National Civil Aviation Agency (ANAC), the UK Department for Transport, the African Civil Aviation Commission (AFCAC), and the Arab Civil Aviation Organisation.

Representing Egypt and the Arab Group, Gamil emphasised that the success of the global transition in aviation requires taking into account the different economic and development circumstances of individual countries when designing international and regional policies. He also highlighted the importance of technology transfer, capacity building, access to financing, and encouraging investment to ensure a balanced and practical transition while maintaining the competitiveness of the air transport sector.

The discussions focused on a number of political, regulatory, and economic issues, particularly how to develop policies that provide investors with the necessary certainty, determine the appropriate timing for introducing regulatory requirements, address differences in countries’ capabilities, ensure the availability of sustainable aviation fuel at competitive prices, and strike a balance between the interests of fuel producers and airlines.

text:
By Faith Anisiobi, The Sight News

The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA) has commenced discussions with the African Aviation and Aerospace University (AAAU), Abuja, on strengthening technical capacity, knowledge development and professional expertise to support the emerging Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) ecosystem in Nigeria.

The discussions were held when a technical team from the NCAA Environment Team, including NCAA SAF Technical Expert and ICAO Consultant, Jon McKechnie, visited AAAU to explore collaboration on SAF development, training, knowledge exchange and institutional capacity building.

The team was received by the Acting Vice-Chancellor of AAAU, Dr Mustapha Sheikh Abdullahi, alongside members of the university management and staff.

Abdullahi highlighted AAAU’s academic programmes and growing focus on aviation, aerospace and environmental sustainability, as well as the role of the African Centre for Climate Change and Aviation Decarbonization (ACCCAD) in advancing research, knowledge and capacity development in climate change and aviation decarbonization.

He said the engagement built on preliminary efforts initiated in 2025 to explore Nigeria’s potential for SAF development, noting that studies had identified significant opportunities for SAF production from available sustainable resources.

According to him, attention is now shifting towards translating the identified potential into practical action, including developing the technical, academic and institutional capacity required for a functional SAF ecosystem.

Abdullahi said AAAU could serve as a knowledge and training base for SAF capacity development, particularly through the proposed Training of Trainers (ToT) programme.

He explained that the programme is designed to develop a pool of professionals and subject-matter experts capable of transferring knowledge and supporting broader capacity development in the SAF sector.

The Acting Vice-Chancellor expressed the university’s interest in hosting and supporting SAF-related training and knowledge-development activities, adding that the collaboration could also strengthen ACCCAD’s technical foundation and broader capacity-development objectives.

The NCAA team discussed the structure and requirements of the proposed programme, including the technical and knowledge areas to be covered and the academic foundation needed to support the initiative.

The team also explored opportunities for exchanges involving tutors, trainers and subject-matter experts among relevant institutions, as well as the infrastructure required to develop, absorb and transfer knowledge in the emerging SAF field.

The NCAA emphasized the importance of collaboration among regulators, academic institutions, technical experts, industry stakeholders and other partners, given the multidisciplinary nature of SAF development.

It was agreed that the leadership of ACCCAD and other relevant experts at AAAU would work with the NCAA technical team to further define areas of collaboration, including training, subject-matter expertise, knowledge exchange and the proposed Training of Trainers programme.

The engagement is expected to contribute to strengthening Nigeria’s human and institutional capacity for its Sustainable Aviation Fuel ambitions and deepen collaboration between the aviation regulator and academia towards a more sustainable, lower-emission aviation sector.

title: Spain Tourism 2030 Puts Residents and Businesses at the Heart of a New Sustainable Travel Era
description:
Spain Moves From Tourism Strategy to Implementation The Spanish government approved the Spain Tourism 2030 Strategy in October 2025 after a participatory process involving public administrations, tourism businesses, social organisations and other stakeholders.
Its five main areas cover destinations, businesses, tourism workers, residents and tourists.
Businesses Will Have a Larger Role in Sustainable Tourism Tourism companies are another central part of the 2030 framework.
More Attention on Rural and Inland Spain Spain’s tourism strategy also aims to reduce the concentration of travel around traditional hotspots.
What the Changes Could Mean for Travellers For travellers, Spain Tourism 2030 is unlikely to mean an immediate overhaul of holidays.
text:
Spain, Madrid, Barcelona and Málaga are entering a new phase of tourism planning as the country moves to put residents, businesses, workers and travellers at the centre of its Tourism 2030 strategy. For visitors, the change could eventually mean a different kind of Spanish holiday — one that puts greater emphasis on less-crowded destinations, local communities, responsible travel and experiences beyond the country’s busiest tourist hotspots.

Spain Moves From Tourism Strategy to Implementation

The Spanish government approved the Spain Tourism 2030 Strategy in October 2025 after a participatory process involving public administrations, tourism businesses, social organisations and other stakeholders.

Rather than measuring tourism only by visitor numbers and spending, the strategy takes a broader approach built around three forms of sustainability: economic, social and environmental.

The framework contains 50 measures and 148 concrete instruments, involving 18 of Spain’s 22 ministries. Its five main areas cover destinations, businesses, tourism workers, residents and tourists.

The strategy has now moved beyond planning. Spain’s Ministry of Industry and Tourism says implementation has begun on 45% of the 148 instruments, while the government prepares its 2026–2027 Biennial Plan to prioritise measures over the next two years.

Residents Become Part of Spain’s Tourism Model

One of the most notable changes is the government’s decision to treat residents as a central part of tourism policy.

The strategy seeks to strengthen social cohesion, balance tourism with the use of public spaces and protect local culture and heritage. It also aims to improve the relationship between visitors and the communities that host them.

This approach comes as Spain continues to experience exceptionally strong international tourism demand. The country received 11.5 million international tourists in July 2026, an increase of 4.6% from July 2025. During the first seven months of the year, more than 58.1 million international visitors travelled to Spain, also representing 4.6% growth year on year.

For communities in highly visited destinations, managing that growth is becoming increasingly important.

A New Focus on Tourism Pressure and Visitor Flows

Spain is developing an Atlas of Tourism Intensity to provide better information about visitor flows and tourism pressure.

The government says the tool is intended to support decision-making and improve coexistence between tourism and local life. The wider strategy also includes measures designed to improve the management of destinations, public resources and tourist flows.

For travellers, this could gradually change how popular destinations manage demand.

Instead of concentrating visitors in the same cities, beaches and attractions, Spain wants tourism to become more geographically and seasonally distributed.

That creates an opportunity for lesser-known Spanish destinations to receive greater attention while established hotspots face less pressure.

Businesses Will Have a Larger Role in Sustainable Tourism

Tourism companies are another central part of the 2030 framework.

Spain’s strategy calls for greater innovation and digitalisation, stronger responsible-business practices and the development of a circular economy within tourism.

Small and medium-sized tourism businesses are particularly important to this transition, with government programmes designed to improve their digital capabilities and competitiveness.

The objective is not simply to bring more visitors into Spain. It is to create a tourism economy where businesses can generate value while destinations and communities also benefit.

That distinction could become increasingly important as travellers become more interested in locally rooted and environmentally responsible experiences.

More Attention on Rural and Inland Spain

Spain’s tourism strategy also aims to reduce the concentration of travel around traditional hotspots.

The government wants to promote green and inland tourism, encourage geographic diversification and strengthen destinations outside the country’s busiest tourist centres. Its tourism programme also includes responsible marketing intended to spread demand across different destinations and periods of the year.

For international visitors, that could mean greater visibility for rural communities, inland cities, cultural destinations and nature-based experiences.

Instead of travelling only during the busiest summer months, visitors could increasingly be encouraged to explore Spain during shoulder and off-peak periods.

Strong Tourist Demand Makes the Shift More Urgent

Spain’s tourism boom shows why the government is focusing on how growth is managed.

International tourist expenditure reached €18.218 billion in July 2026, increasing 10.9% compared with the same month a year earlier. Average expenditure per visitor rose 5.9% to €1,579, while average daily expenditure reached €218.

During the first seven months of 2026, international tourist spending reached €82.054 billion, up 7.8% year on year.

These figures underline the economic importance of tourism while also highlighting why Spain is looking beyond simple visitor growth.

Sustainability Extends to Aviation and Climate Resilience

Spain’s tourism transition is also reaching transportation.

The government’s 2026–2027 implementation work includes energy-efficiency measures, climate adaptation and support for Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) as part of efforts to reduce emissions from tourism-related air travel.

The strategy also calls for destinations to become more resilient to climate change while improving the environmental management of tourism.

This matters for international travel because Spain remains heavily dependent on air connectivity, particularly for visitors arriving from long-haul and European markets.

What the Changes Could Mean for Travellers

For travellers, Spain Tourism 2030 is unlikely to mean an immediate overhaul of holidays.

Instead, the changes are likely to emerge gradually through destination management, marketing, accommodation policies, digital tourism services and efforts to spread visitor demand.

Travellers may increasingly encounter recommendations that steer them toward lesser-known destinations, off-season travel and experiences connected with local culture and communities.

The strategy also encourages responsible marketing and greater environmental and social awareness among tourists, making the visitor an active participant in Spain’s future tourism model rather than simply a consumer.

Spain Wants Tourism Growth Without Losing Its Appeal

The challenge for Spain is balancing two realities: tourism is an enormous economic engine, but the country’s most popular destinations also have to remain liveable for residents.

The government’s current approach attempts to address both sides by giving residents a formal place in tourism planning while continuing to support businesses, workers and international visitors.

With millions more travellers continuing to arrive and billions of euros flowing into the economy, Spain’s Tourism 2030 strategy represents an attempt to redefine what successful tourism looks like.

For travellers, that could ultimately mean a Spain that asks them to look beyond the familiar — to discover quieter places, travel at different times of the year and experience destinations in ways that create value not only for visitors, but also for the people who call them home.

text:
NewsVoir

Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], September 26: DHL Express, the world's leading international express services provider, announced price adjustments today that will take effect on January 1, 2027. The increase in India will be 8.9%.

"International trade continues to create new opportunities for businesses, while supply chains are becoming increasingly interconnected and complex," said R S Subramanian, SVP, South Asia, DHL Express. "We remain committed to helping our customers navigate this evolving environment by investing in our global network, digital capabilities, security infrastructure, and sustainable logistics solutions. This annual price adjustment enables us to maintain the high level of service and reliability our customers expect while continuing to strengthen the resilience and adaptability of our global operations."

DHL Express adjusts its prices annually to account for inflationary pressures, currency fluctuations, and industry-specific cost developments. As an internationally integrated business operating in more than 220 countries and territories, DHL Express is influenced not only by local economic conditions but also by developments across global markets.

In addition to inflation, the company's cost structure continues to be affected by factors such as energy costs, compliance requirements, and administrative expenses related to evolving customs, regulatory, and security measures introduced by national and international authorities. Ongoing labor market pressures in many countries also contribute to increased operational costs.

text: Sustainability LIVE London 2026 in London... with Riku Aho on Scaling Sustainable Aviation Fuel & Direct Mitigation Strategies. "The issue with offsetting is that when you set climate targets, there's an element of operating ability—offsets might not be as credible as something that's based on science." Key Takeaways: • Why direct mitigation through science-based targets provides far greater credibility and impact than traditional carbon offsetting. • How European SAF mandates are accelerating the commercial scaling and adoption of sustainable fuels for airlines. • How combining fleet renewal with operational tactics like continuous descent approaches drives meaningful, immediate fuel savings. "Riku Aho is a Vice President of Sustainability at Finnair, bringing nearly 16 years of aviation experience—spanning aircraft trading, leasing, and corporate sustainability—to the conversation. His deep background in both commercial fleet operations and environmental strategy makes his perspective on decarbonization targets and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) integration highly authoritative. In this exclusive interview, Riku outlines Finnair's strategic transition away from traditional carbon offsetting in favor of direct mitigation measures aligned with Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) standards. He details how the airline has progressively integrated Sustainable Aviation Fuel into its operations, noting a major scale-up following the implementation of the European SAF Mandate in early 2025. Beyond SAF, Riku breaks down the secondary levers required to drive meaningful decarbonization across commercial aviation. He highlights Finnair's ongoing fleet renewal program, including the recent refresh of their narrowbody fleet and the high-efficiency performance of their modern Airbus A350 widebody aircraft, which account for the vast majority of the airline's fuel burn. Finally, the discussion dives into operational micro-efficiencies that collectively deliver major fuel savings. Riku highlights Finnair's focus on weight reduction and operational optimization, detailing practical tactics such as single-engine taxiing, minimizing APU usage, utilizing preconditioned air at gates, and leveraging continuous descent operations into hubs like Helsinki to glide aircraft down at peak fuel efficiency." title: Nitin Gadkari: માત્ર ખાંડ વેચવાથી નહીં ભરાય તિજોરી! ગડકરીએ બતાવ્યો નવી ફોર્મ્યુલા
description:
હાલમાં, ખાંડના વધતા ભાવે સામાન્ય માણસના રસોડાના બજેટને ખોરવી નાખ્યું છે.
જોકે, જો ખાંડની મિલો તેમની આવક માત્ર ખાંડના વેચાણ પૂરતી જ મર્યાદિત રાખે, તો નફાકારકતા જાળવી રાખવી મુશ્કેલ બનશે.
ખાંડ મિલોને નીતિન ગડકરીની સલાહ આ બાબતને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને, કેન્દ્રીય મંત્રી નીતિન ગડકરીએ મિલોને નવી દિશામાં પગલાં લેવાની સલાહ આપી છે.
અન્ય ઉત્પાદનોના ઉત્પાદન પર ધ્યાન : નીતિન ગડકરી નીતિન ગડકરીનું કહેવું છે કે મિલોએ ખાંડ સિવાયની અન્ય વસ્તુઓ જેમ કે ઇથેનોલ, ટકાઉ ઉડ્ડયન ઇંધણ (sustainable aviation fuel) અને જૈવ-ખાતરના ઉત્પાદન પર વધુ ભાર મૂકવો જોઈએ.
મિલની આવક વધારવા પર ધ્યાન નીતિન ગડકરીએ એ પણ પ્રકાશિત કર્યું કે શેરડીના કૂચા (bagasse) અને અન્ય કૃષિ કચરામાંથી CBG જેવા ઇંધણનું ઉત્પાદન કરી શકાય છે.
text:
ખાંડ એ દરેક ઘરની દૈનિક જરૂરિયાતોમાંની એક મુખ્ય વસ્તુ છે. હાલમાં, ખાંડના વધતા ભાવે સામાન્ય માણસના રસોડાના બજેટને ખોરવી નાખ્યું છે. જોકે, જો ખાંડની મિલો તેમની આવક માત્ર ખાંડના વેચાણ પૂરતી જ મર્યાદિત રાખે, તો નફાકારકતા જાળવી રાખવી મુશ્કેલ બનશે.

ખાંડ મિલોને નીતિન ગડકરીની સલાહ

આ બાબતને ધ્યાનમાં રાખીને, કેન્દ્રીય મંત્રી નીતિન ગડકરીએ મિલોને નવી દિશામાં પગલાં લેવાની સલાહ આપી છે. તેમણે ભારપૂર્વક જણાવ્યું છે કે માત્ર ખાંડના વેચાણ પર નિર્ભર રહેવું પૂરતું નથી અને અન્ય ઉત્પાદનોના ઉત્પાદન પર પણ ધ્યાન કેન્દ્રિત કરવા અનુરોધ કર્યો છે.કેન્દ્રીય મંત્રી નીતિન ગડકરીએ ખાંડની મિલોને માત્ર ખાંડના ઉત્પાદન અને વેચાણ પૂરતું સીમિત ન રહેવા, પરંતુ શેરડી અને તેમાંથી ઉત્પન્ન થતા કચરાનો પણ ઉપયોગ કરવા જણાવ્યું છે.

અન્ય ઉત્પાદનોના ઉત્પાદન પર ધ્યાન : નીતિન ગડકરી

નીતિન ગડકરીનું કહેવું છે કે મિલોએ ખાંડ સિવાયની અન્ય વસ્તુઓ જેમ કે ઇથેનોલ, ટકાઉ ઉડ્ડયન ઇંધણ (sustainable aviation fuel) અને જૈવ-ખાતરના ઉત્પાદન પર વધુ ભાર મૂકવો જોઈએ.

અન્ય દેશો પરની નિર્ભરતા ઘટાડવા પર ધ્યાન

મધ્ય પૂર્વમાં તણાવને કારણે દેશમાં પેટ્રોલ અને ડીઝલના પુરવઠા પર અસર પડી હતી, જેના પગલે સરકારે ક્રૂડ ઓઈલની આયાત પરની નિર્ભરતા ઘટાડવા માટે 'ઇથેનોલ બ્લેન્ડિંગ' (પેટ્રોલમાં ઇથેનોલનું મિશ્રણ) પર ધ્યાન કેન્દ્રિત કર્યું છે. પરિણામે, E20 પેટ્રોલના પ્રચારને સમર્થન આપવા માટે ઇથેનોલની માંગમાં વધારો થયો છે.

ગડકરીએ નોંધ્યું હતું કે કૃષિ અને અન્ય જૈવિક કચરામાંથી CBG (કોમ્પ્રેસ્ડ બાયોગેસ)નું ઉત્પાદન ગેસ, પેટ્રોલ અને ડીઝલ માટે વિદેશી રાષ્ટ્રો પરની નિર્ભરતા ઘટાડવામાં નોંધપાત્ર મદદ કરી શકે છે. તેનો અર્થ સ્પષ્ટ છે: જો ખાંડની મિલો તેમનું ધ્યાન ખાંડના ઉત્પાદનથી આગળ વધીને ઇથેનોલ અને CBGના ઉત્પાદન તરફ વાળે, તો તેઓ તેમની આવકમાં વધારો કરી શકે છે, જેનો અંતે ખેડૂતોને પણ લાભ થશે.

મિલની આવક વધારવા પર ધ્યાન

નીતિન ગડકરીએ એ પણ પ્રકાશિત કર્યું કે શેરડીના કૂચા (bagasse) અને અન્ય કૃષિ કચરામાંથી CBG જેવા ઇંધણનું ઉત્પાદન કરી શકાય છે. તેનો સૌથી મોટો ફાયદો મિલોની આવકમાં સંભવિત વધારો થશે. વધુમાં, ખેડૂતોને પણ તેમની શેરડી માટે ઊંચો ભાવ મળી શકે છે.

text:
Pilatus Aircraft informa: “Un cockpit completamente nuovo basato sul Garmin G3000 PRIME Integrated Flight Deck, dotato di funzionalità come Safety Autoland, rende il nuovo PC-12 PRO l’aereo tecnologicamente più avanzato, con le migliori performance e più affidabile della sua categoria. Il Safety Autoland system è stato certificato sia dall’European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) che dalla Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

Il PC-12 si colloca già tra gli aerei più sicuri della categoria, con un record di sicurezza eccezionale e statisticamente provato. Con il PC-12 PRO, Pilatus porta questo eccellente standard di sicurezza a un livello ancora più elevato: l’ultima generazione di questo bestseller è dotata di una serie di funzioni di sicurezza aggiuntive, incluso l’innovativo Safety Autoland system. Durante i final certification flights, Safety Autoland è stato al centro dell’attenzione poiché è stato sottoposto a test approfonditi. L’obiettivo era dimostrare un fully automated landing in real-world conditions, dall’attivazione del sistema fino all’atterraggio sicuro, alla comunicazione automatizzata e all’engine shutdown”.

“Safety Autoland è progettato per gestire situazioni che comportano l’improvvisa pilot incapacitation, ad esempio a causa di un’emergenza medica. Quando viene premuto il pulsante di attivazione o quando viene rilevata l’inattività del pilota, il sistema prende il pieno controllo dell’aereo, informando tutti gli occupanti che l’automated landing mode è stata attivata. Contemporaneamente, inizia ad analizzare tutte le informazioni disponibili, comprese le condizioni meteorologiche, l’aircraft status e i navigation data.

Sulla base di queste informazioni, il sistema determina la scelta migliore per l’aeroporto, tenendo conto di fattori quali la lunghezza della pista, il vento, le condizioni meteorologiche e il carburante rimanente. Quindi calcola un percorso sicuro, evitando ostacoli e terreno. Durante il volo autonomo, Safety Autoland si prende cura di tutti i sistemi necessari per l’atterraggio – inclusi flaps, landing gear, lighting and de-icing – e prepara completamente l’aereo per l’avvicinamento finale. Gestisce inoltre tutte le comunicazioni radio, effettuando automaticamente chiamate sulle frequenze appropriate per tenere informati sulla situazione l’ATC e le persone a terra”, prosegue Pilatus Aircraft.

“In un single-engine aircraft, un propulsore collaudato è il componente più importante. Il PC-12 PRO è equipaggiato con l’ultima versione dell’aircraft engine più affidabile mai costruito: il Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6. Con oltre 60.000 unità in servizio e più di 400 milioni di ore in volo, la famiglia di motori PT6 vanta un track record senza eguali.

Inoltre, il PC-12 PRO produce meno emissioni di CO2 rispetto ai twin-engine turboprops comparabili e può funzionare con sustainable aviation fuel (SAF blends), consentendo un volo più sostenibile senza perdita di prestazioni.

Tutte queste innovazioni fanno sì che il nuovo PC-12 PRO sia l’aereo tecnologicamente più avanzato, più performante e più affidabile della sua categoria. Il PC-12 PRO è stato ripensato, ma è immediatamente riconoscibile. In breve: il Most Advanced Single è arrivato”, conclude Pilatus Aircraft

title: China Southern Airlines Celebrates 70 Years Of Connecting The World As Mid-Autumn ...
description:
The celebration reflected China Southern Airlines’ transformation from a regional carrier based in Guangzhou into one of the world’s largest airlines with an extensive international network.
From Guangzhou To The World Through Seven Decades Of Aviation Growth China Southern Airlines’ growth story reflects the rapid evolution of global aviation over the past 70 years.
Beyond New York, China Southern provides direct services linking Guangzhou with key destinations in North America, including Los Angeles, San Francisco, Toronto and Vancouver.
In 2025, China Southern Airlines carried 174 million passengers across its network.
Through seven decades of development, China Southern Airlines has grown alongside the changing needs of global travellers.
text:
China Southern Airlines has marked two major cultural and aviation milestones with a special celebration on the world-famous digital screens of Times Square in New York, highlighting the airline’s 70-year journey and the timeless message of reunion represented by the Mid-Autumn Festival.

The landmark display brought together aviation achievement and cultural heritage, showcasing how air travel has become a powerful link between communities, economies and cultures across continents. The celebration reflected China Southern Airlines’ transformation from a regional carrier based in Guangzhou into one of the world’s largest airlines with an extensive international network.

For seven decades, China Southern Airlines has developed its operations around the idea of making global travel more accessible while maintaining a strong focus on safety, service quality and passenger experience. From its beginnings in southern China, the airline has expanded its reach to connect major cities, business centres and cultural destinations worldwide.

The anniversary celebration also carried special significance as it coincided with the Mid-Autumn Festival, a traditional Chinese holiday centred around family reunion, appreciation and togetherness. The festival, celebrated under the full moon, represents the importance of maintaining connections despite physical distances.

From Guangzhou To The World Through Seven Decades Of Aviation Growth

China Southern Airlines’ growth story reflects the rapid evolution of global aviation over the past 70 years. Operating from its major hub in Guangzhou, the airline has built an international network that supports tourism, trade, business travel and cultural exchange.

The carrier’s expanding global presence has helped create stronger links between China and international markets. This year also marks 12 years since the launch of its direct New York–Guangzhou service, strengthening connections between two major global cities.

Beyond New York, China Southern provides direct services linking Guangzhou with key destinations in North America, including Los Angeles, San Francisco, Toronto and Vancouver. These routes support growing travel demand while creating new opportunities for international visitors, businesses and communities.

The airline’s wider network now extends across 177 countries and regions, reaching more than 1,000 destinations worldwide. Through this extensive connectivity, China Southern continues to play a role in supporting global mobility and strengthening links between different cultures.

A Modern Fleet Supporting Global Travel Expansion

Behind China Southern Airlines’ international network is one of the largest aircraft fleets in the aviation industry. By the end of 2025, the airline operated 972 aircraft, including advanced models from major manufacturers.

The fleet includes Boeing 787 and Boeing 777 aircraft, Airbus A350 and Airbus A330 wide-body aircraft, along with domestically developed C909 and C919 aircraft. These aircraft support both long-haul international operations and regional connectivity, helping the airline serve millions of passengers each year.

In 2025, China Southern Airlines carried 174 million passengers across its network. The airline also recorded an on-time performance rate of 91.01%, reflecting its focus on operational efficiency and reliable service.

Safety remains a central part of the airline’s long-term development. China Southern has maintained more than 30 million consecutive hours of safe flight operations, demonstrating its continued commitment to aviation safety standards and responsible air transport.

Bringing Chinese Culture And Local Flavours Into The Flying Experience

Beyond transportation, China Southern Airlines has focused on creating a more personalised travel experience through initiatives that combine hospitality, culture and regional identity.

The airline’s “Gourmet Southern Airlines” programme introduces passengers to diverse flavours and culinary traditions while travelling. The initiative highlights regional cuisine, improved onboard services and cultural elements designed to make journeys more memorable.

Passengers can experience food inspired by different regions while enjoying refreshed cabin amenities and family-friendly travel activities. These efforts reflect the airline’s broader approach of making air travel more than just a journey between two locations.

By incorporating cultural experiences into its services, China Southern aims to create stronger emotional connections with travellers while showcasing the diversity of Chinese traditions to international passengers.

Moving Towards A Greener And More Sustainable Aviation Future

As global aviation continues to focus on environmental responsibility, China Southern Airlines is advancing measures designed to support a more sustainable future for air travel.

The airline is exploring the use of sustainable aviation fuel, improving fuel efficiency through modern aircraft operations and reducing waste throughout its services. Additional sustainability initiatives include carbon-footprint-labelled meals, environmentally responsible catering practices and biodegradable alternatives to traditional single-use plastics.

These efforts form part of a wider transformation across the aviation sector, where airlines are working to balance growing travel demand with environmental goals.

China Southern’s sustainability strategy reflects the changing expectations of modern travellers, who increasingly seek more responsible and environmentally conscious travel options.

Times Square Celebration Highlights The Power Of Travel Connections

The appearance of China Southern Airlines on Times Square’s giant LED screens represented more than an anniversary celebration. It highlighted the role of aviation in bringing distant communities closer together.

The timing with the Mid-Autumn Festival added another layer of meaning, as the holiday is traditionally associated with reunion and maintaining bonds between families and loved ones separated by distance.

Through seven decades of development, China Southern Airlines has grown alongside the changing needs of global travellers. Its expanding network, modern fleet, safety record and cultural initiatives demonstrate the continuing evolution of international air connectivity.

From Guangzhou to New York and from China to destinations around the world, every flight represents a connection between people, places and experiences. The airline’s 70th anniversary celebration reflects both its aviation achievements and its ongoing role in supporting global movement in the years ahead.

title: Airbus Forecasts Middle East Airlines Will Need 3,830 New Passenger Aircraft By 2045
description:
Middle East: Middle Eastern airlines are expected to require 3,830 new passenger aircraft by 2045, according to Airbus’ latest Global Market Forecast, as rising air travel demand, population growth, urbanisation and major investments in airlines and airports drive long-term fleet expansion.
Gabriel Semelas, President of Airbus Africa and Middle East, said regional airlines were showing operational resilience despite geopolitical volatility.
Airbus forecasts that new-generation aircraft will account for 97% of the Middle East fleet by 2035, compared with 45% in 2025.
The Middle East is also expected to play a growing role in the development of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF).
The Middle East aircraft forecast therefore combines fleet replacement with additional capacity required for higher passenger demand.
text:
Middle East: Middle Eastern airlines are expected to require 3,830 new passenger aircraft by 2045, according to Airbus’ latest Global Market Forecast, as rising air travel demand, population growth, urbanisation and major investments in airlines and airports drive long-term fleet expansion.

The forecast calls for 2,160 single-aisle aircraft and 1,670 widebody aircraft over the next 20 years. Airbus expects passenger traffic to, from and within the Middle East to grow at an average annual rate of 4.7%, more than doubling by 2045. The 3,830-aircraft figure represents projected market demand and is not a tally of confirmed aircraft orders. Existing Middle Eastern backlogs for large single-aisle aircraft already cover about 45% of the region’s projected 20-year demand.

Gabriel Semelas, President of Airbus Africa and Middle East, said regional airlines were showing operational resilience despite geopolitical volatility. He said demographic growth, rising prosperity and major infrastructure investment were supporting fleet expansion and modernisation while the region moves towards more efficient and sustainable air transport.

Airbus expects the region’s growth to be supported by rising disposable incomes, greater urbanisation and a substantial expansion of the middle class. The Middle Eastern middle-class population is forecast to increase by 240 million to 620 million by 2045, while urbanisation is expected to reach 55% of the population.

Air travel frequency is also projected to increase significantly. In Saudi Arabia, annual air trips per person are forecast to rise from 1.6 in 2025 to 4.0 in 2045. In the UAE, the figure is expected to increase from 3.1 to 6.5 trips per person over the same period. Airbus said the figures represent projected travel frequency rather than the number of aircraft individual countries will purchase.

Fleet renewal will be another major component of the projected aircraft demand. Airbus forecasts that new-generation aircraft will account for 97% of the Middle East fleet by 2035, compared with 45% in 2025.

The manufacturer said the shift towards newer aircraft would improve fuel efficiency and operating performance while supporting reductions in emissions. The Middle East is therefore expected to experience one of the faster fleet-modernisation rates as airlines replace older aircraft while adding capacity for expanding networks.

The regional outlook also comes as Middle Eastern carriers continue to place significant aircraft orders. In May 2026, Saudia became the first airline in the Middle East and Africa to receive an Airbus A321XLR, with 15 A321XLRs on order. In July 2026, Saudi low-cost carrier flynas agreed to acquire five additional A330-900s and 20 additional A321neos, taking its firm Airbus commitment to 235 aircraft.

Airbus said multi-billion-dollar investments in airlines, airport infrastructure and regional giga-projects are reshaping the Middle East’s aviation network. The investments are creating additional connectivity hubs and supporting growth across the wider aviation ecosystem.

The forecast comes as Airbus expects aviation networks globally to become more decentralised over the next two decades. Globally, Airbus forecasts demand for 42,060 new aircraft between 2026 and 2045, including 33,920 typically single-aisle aircraft and 8,140 typically widebody aircraft. Of the total, 22,240 aircraft are required for fleet growth and 19,820 for replacement of older aircraft. Global passenger traffic is forecast to grow by 3.9% annually, reaching about 10 billion passengers per year by 2045.

The Middle East is also expected to play a growing role in the development of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF). Airbus said sovereign investment strategies and regional aviation programmes are positioning Middle Eastern airlines and other stakeholders to become potential hubs for future SAF production.

The company did not provide a specific regional SAF production volume or a firm timeline for individual projects in the forecast.

The Middle East aircraft forecast therefore combines fleet replacement with additional capacity required for higher passenger demand. Airbus’ outlook indicates that airlines will increasingly rely on newer-generation single-aisle and widebody aircraft as the region expands its international connectivity, airport infrastructure and aviation-related investment through 2045.

title: Flattery won't fix the challenges facing air travel
authors: Robert Silk, culture or relaxation, we looked at hotels
description:
On Sept. 2, American Airlines CEO Robert Isom stood before President Trump in the Oval Office, where Trump was hosting a gathering of travel industry leaders.
For that record revenue quarter, American reported operating income of just $446 million, down from $1.14 billion a year earlier.
There's no doubt the Trump administration has taken some steps that are beneficial to U.S. airlines.
Those changes might not benefit the travel industry and travelers overall, but they'll please airlines.
Net profit among North American airlines would drop to $9.4 billion this year, down $3 billion from last year.
text:
On Sept. 2, American Airlines CEO Robert Isom stood before President Trump in the Oval Office, where Trump was hosting a gathering of travel industry leaders.

Smiling broadly, Isom made a reference to "records at American" and record levels of traffic for the airline industry, which he said were no doubt due to the economy and the job market.

"So, thank you, Mr. President," he said, looking every bit like a kid in a candy shop.

I'm not sure what industry traffic records Isom was referring to. An analysis by the travel blog Johnny Jet of TSA throughput statistics from June 21 to the Sept. 7 end of the Labor Day travel period found a drop of 5.8 million passengers, a 2.7% year-over-year decline. When I asked, an American spokeswoman said the airline broke its own 2019 record this summer for total flyers from Memorial Day through Labor Day. American also set its all-time single-quarter revenue record in Q2, at $16.7 billion.

Still, American's overall results have not been stellar. Its expenses grew 22.9% in Q2, due in large part to a $2.2 billion increase in fuel expenses driven by the Iran war.

For that record revenue quarter, American reported operating income of just $446 million, down from $1.14 billion a year earlier. For the full year, American predicted break even results in July, before fuel prices jumped about $1 per gallon in the late summer.

There's no doubt the Trump administration has taken some steps that are beneficial to U.S. airlines. Most notably, its commitment to modernizing the U.S. air traffic control system hopefully will pay dividends for airlines and travelers, even assuming it takes longer than DOT secretary Sean Duffy's aggressive timeline of completion by 2028. Last year Congress funded the overhaul with $12.5 billion; Duffy is pushing for another $30 billion.

The administration has also been friendly to the airline industry's deregulatory agenda. For example, it chose not to fight against an industry lawsuit that successfully killed the Biden-era regulation that would have required airlines to display bag and change fees at the start of a fare inquiry. And beginning next month, a new DOT rule will grant more exceptions to the requirement that airlines provide refunds for canceled or delayed flights. Those changes might not benefit the travel industry and travelers overall, but they'll please airlines.

But broader administration policies have also inflicted substantial harm on airlines. Trump's tariffs, and his generally bellicose approach to U.S. allies, were undoubtedly the driving force behind inbound U.S. tourism declining by 5.5% in 2025, to the substantial detriment of airlines.

Meanwhile, IATA estimated in its most recent financial forecast, issued in June, that the Iran war would lead to $98 billion in extra global jet fuel costs this year. Net profit among North American airlines would drop to $9.4 billion this year, down $3 billion from last year. U.S. jet fuel prices have increased around 50% since IATA issued that forecast, making those estimates now sound optimistic.

I realize that what an airline CEO says on television to a president who's known to target businesses and individuals who challenge him isn't necessarily reflective of what happens behind closed doors.

But I'm hoping that somewhere beyond my vision, Isom, airlines and the travel industry writ large are mixing flattery of Trump with something more real: honest assessments of the heavy toll some of his policies are exacting on traveler counts and bottom lines.

title: Top Middle East leaders - Kamil Al-Awadhi International Air Transport Association
description:
As the International Air Transport Association’s regional vice president for Africa and the Middle East, he represents airlines across a region of global hubs, fast-growing markets and persistent structural constraints.
The liberalization of African air transport can widen opportunity, but only if governments translate agreements into permissions, infrastructure and predictable rules.
Sustainable aviation fuel, more efficient aircraft, air traffic modernization and credible carbon frameworks will require cooperation far beyond individual carriers.
Al-Awadhi can frame the matter through the practical decisions an airline chief executive must make, not only through institutional principle.
A Gulf network carrier, an African start-up and a European airline serving the region will not agree on every policy.
text:
Kamil Al-Awadhi occupies one of aviation’s most consequential intermediary positions. As the International Air Transport Association’s regional vice president for Africa and the Middle East, he represents airlines across a region of global hubs, fast-growing markets and persistent structural constraints. His task is not to run a carrier but to improve the conditions in which many carriers operate, making the case for regulation, infrastructure and charges that support safe, competitive connectivity.

He took up the role in 2021 after more than three decades in aviation. Most notably, he served as chief executive of Kuwait Airways, giving him first-hand experience of the financial, political and operational pressures faced by a national airline. Earlier responsibilities spanned safety, security, quality management and enterprise systems. His academic grounding, including engineering studies in aircraft maintenance management and an MBA in aerospace management from Toulouse, reinforces a career built across both the technical and commercial sides of the business.

That breadth shapes his agenda at IATA. Africa and the Middle East cannot be treated as one uniform aviation market. Gulf hubs possess world-class infrastructure and powerful network airlines. Parts of Africa still contend with high taxes, weak connectivity, blocked airline funds, uneven safety outcomes and limited implementation of liberalization commitments. Al-Awadhi’s value lies in moving between those realities without reducing either to slogans.

His public priorities have consistently included safety, connectivity, sustainability and cost competitiveness. Each is interdependent. Better airspace management reduces delay, fuel burn and emissions. Rational airport and government charges make marginal routes more viable. Common standards and effective regulation build confidence. The liberalization of African air transport can widen opportunity, but only if governments translate agreements into permissions, infrastructure and predictable rules.

Al-Awadhi also serves as a translator between airlines and states. Governments understandably see aviation as a source of revenue, strategic influence and national pride. Airlines see a thin-margin system in which poorly designed fees or fragmented regulation can erase route economics. Because he has led an airline, his advocacy carries operational credibility. He can explain not only that a policy is burdensome, but how it changes schedules, fleet deployment, ticket prices and investment decisions.

The sustainability challenge makes that dialogue more urgent. The region is expanding capacity while the global industry pursues net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. Sustainable aviation fuel, more efficient aircraft, air traffic modernization and credible carbon frameworks will require cooperation far beyond individual carriers. IATA’s regional office must keep ambitious policy connected to technological and commercial reality. Al-Awadhi’s engineering and management background is particularly relevant here.

His leadership is best understood as enabling rather than theatrical. When industry representation works, passengers rarely see it. They experience safer operations, more direct routes, fewer regulatory frictions and prices that reflect genuine cost rather than avoidable inefficiency. Al-Awadhi has made those underlying systems his field of influence. In a region where aviation is both infrastructure and economic strategy, that quiet work helps determine how widely the benefits of growth are shared.

One persistent issue illustrates the value of his approach: blocked airline funds in markets where carriers cannot repatriate ticket revenues. To a government this can appear as a foreign-exchange measure; to an airline it becomes trapped working capital and a reason to reduce capacity. IATA’s role is to quantify the consequences, maintain dialogue and help authorities find orderly solutions. Al-Awadhi can frame the matter through the practical decisions an airline chief executive must make, not only through institutional principle.

He must also hold together members with different interests. A Gulf network carrier, an African start-up and a European airline serving the region will not agree on every policy. Credible representation depends on identifying common ground while speaking honestly about uneven performance within the industry itself. Al-Awadhi’s mandate is strongest when advocacy is paired with accountability on safety, consumer confidence and climate. That balance turns IATA from a lobbying voice into a partner governments can use.

text:
All seven modules for the second 35 MW electrolyzer have been delivered

Together with the already delivered 20 MW electrolyzer, Petrobrazi total green hydrogen capacity reaches 55 MW

Green hydrogen will be used in refining processes, including in the new SAF/HVO unit under construction at Petrobrazi

OMV Petrom, the largest integrated energy producer in Southeastern Europe, announces the delivery of all seven modules for its second green hydrogen electrolyzer, with a capacity of 35 MW, at the Petrobrazi refinery. Together with the previously announced 20 MW unit, the total installed green hydrogen production capacity at Petrobrazi now amounts to 55 MW.

Radu Căprău, Member of the Executive Board responsible for Refining and Marketing, said:

Reaching 55 MW of green hydrogen production capacity at Petrobrazi is an important step for our refinery.

”Green hydrogen will be used in refinery processes, including for the production of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), contributing to reducing the emissions of these fuels compared with conventional alternatives. We are also advancing the construction of a 250,000-tonne-per-year SAF/HVO facility, which will position OMV Petrom as the first major producer of sustainable fuels in Southeast Europe,”

The second green hydrogen project consists of seven electrolysis modules of 5 MW each supplied by Neuman & Esser (Germany). The modules were delivered to Petrobrazi over the past two months and are being integrated into the refinery infrastructure.

Construction works, logistics, component manufacturing and module assembly at Petrobrazi are carried out by Kraftanlagen Romania, in partnership with local suppliers.

The 35 MW project benefits from approximately EUR 29 million in non-reimbursable financing through Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR).

Once operational, it is estimated to produce approximately 4,700 tonnes of green hydrogen annually from renewable electricity, for the new SAF/HVO unit under construction at Petrobrazi.

The two green hydrogen projects, with a total installed capacity of 55 MW and estimated annual production of approximately 8,000 tonnes, will be used in refining processes, including the production of sustainable SAF and HVO fuels, obtained from vegetable oils and waste oils. These fuels can reduce CO₂ emissions by at least 65% over their entire life cycle and are compatible with existing infrastructure.

title: ANP autoriza Acelen a ampliar em 10,5% capacidade de tratamento de diesel na Bahia
description:
A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) autorizou a Acelen a ampliar a capacidade de tratamento de diesel na refinaria de Mataripe, localizada em São Francisco do Conde, na Bahia.
A portaria destaca que a ampliação não altera a capacidade total de processamento de petróleo de Mataripe, que permanece em 60 mil m³ por dia.
O aumento acompanha uma estratégia da Acelen de elevar a participação de derivados médios no volume produzido em Mataripe.
Dados divulgados pela companhia mostram que diesel S-10, diesel S-500, diesel marítimo e querosene de aviação passaram de 34% da produção da refinaria em 2022 para 40,5% em 2024.
A Refinaria de Mataripe está entre as maiores unidades de refino em operação no país.
text:
A Agência Nacional do Petróleo, Gás Natural e Biocombustíveis (ANP) autorizou a Acelen a ampliar a capacidade de tratamento de diesel na refinaria de Mataripe, localizada em São Francisco do Conde, na Bahia. A autorização, que foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União na quinta-feira (24), permite que a unidade passe de 12,4 mil para 13,7 mil metros cúbicos por dia, aumento de aproximadamente 10,5%.

A portaria destaca que a ampliação não altera a capacidade total de processamento de petróleo de Mataripe, que permanece em 60 mil m³ por dia. A mudança ocorre especificamente na U-37, unidade de hidrodessulfurização utilizada para reduzir o teor de enxofre e adequar o combustível às especificações exigidas para comercialização.

Na autorização anterior da refinaria, publicada pela ANP em agosto de 2024, a U-37 tinha capacidade de 12,4 mil m³ por dia. As capacidades das demais principais unidades industriais permanecem sem alteração no novo ato.

Para efeitos comparativos, em autorização da ANP publicada em outubro de 2021, pouco antes de a Acelen assumir a operação da antiga Refinaria Landulpho Alves, a capacidade nominal da unidade de hidrodessulfurização de diesel era de 11 mil m³ por dia.

O aumento acompanha uma estratégia da Acelen de elevar a participação de derivados médios no volume produzido em Mataripe. Dados divulgados pela companhia mostram que diesel S-10, diesel S-500, diesel marítimo e querosene de aviação passaram de 34% da produção da refinaria em 2022 para 40,5% em 2024.

Em outubro de 2024, a refinaria atingiu recorde mensal de 530 mil metros cúbicos de destilados médios produzidos.

A Refinaria de Mataripe está entre as maiores unidades de refino em operação no país. Segundo dados do Anuário Estatístico da ANP referentes a 2025, divulgados pela Acelen, a unidade processou em média 262,1 mil barris de petróleo por dia e processou 95,1 milhões de barris de petróleo no ano.

Biorrefinaria de SAF da Acelen vai operar na Bahia a partir de 2029

Em maio deste ano, a Acelen divulgou que vai investir US$ 1,5 bilhão construção de sua biorrefinaria de combustíveis renováveis no município de São Francisco do Conde, na Bahia. A nova unidade, que tem previsão de iniciar as operações em 2029, terá capacidade para produzir 1 bilhão de litros anuais de SAF (sustainable aviation fuel) e diesel renovável (HVO) e terá tecnologia HEFA (Hydroprocessed Esters and Fatty Acids), considerada uma das principais rotas tecnológicas globais para a produção de combustíveis renováveis.

Ao todo, a primeira unidade integrada da companhia terá investimento superior a US$ 3 bilhões e contempla o desenvolvimento agroindustrial com plantação, extração e beneficiamento dos coprodutos da macaúba.

Ainda segundo a empresa, a biorrefinaria será construída em uma área industrial do município baiano e tem previsão de gerar até 3,6 mil empregos diretos e indiretos.

O projeto integra produção agrícola, desenvolvimento industrial e tecnologia para produção de combustíveis renováveis avançados a partir de matérias-primas tradicionais, como óleo de soja e UCO, e de macaúba, cultura nativa brasileira com alto potencial para biocombustíveis avançados.

Em julho, a Acelen e a Trafigura comunicaram ao mercado que assinaram um acordo para fornecer matérias-primas e comercializar combustíveis renováveis, que serão produzidos pela biorrefinaria em construção.

Os contratos preveem o fornecimento, pela Trafigura, de aproximadamente 470 mil toneladas por ano de óleo de cozinha usado (UCO), um volume suficiente para produzir aproximadamente 459 milhões de litros de SAF. Em troca, a Trafigura comprará parte da futura produção de SAF, HVO e Nafta Verde (nafta renovável usada na produção de gasolina e plásticos renováveis), destinados principalmente aos mercados da América do Norte e Europa.

Todos os produtos comercializados sob o acordo atenderão aos padrões internacionais de sustentabilidade e rastreabilidade exigidos pelos principais mercados globais, incluindo certificações como ISCC EU e os requisitos estabelecidos pela Agência de Proteção Ambiental dos EUA (EPA).

Quick Financial Overview

American Airlines Group Inc. has been grinding higher on the chart, not exploding. Over the last few weeks, AAL has climbed from the low $12s to a recent close near $13.87, with multiple tight-range days between $12.90 and $13.60. That slow, stair-step action tells traders accumulation is happening, not a wild short squeeze.

Intraday, AAL’s 5‑minute tape shows a strong close near the highs, with the stock holding above $13.80 into the end of the session. Dips toward $13.40–$13.50 kept getting bought, which is exactly what momentum traders want to see when planning dip buys versus clear support.

Margins are thin — operating margin is only a few percent — but they are positive in a tough fuel environment. The balance sheet is heavy, with roughly $64.2B in assets and about $68.2B in liabilities, so AAL remains a leveraged airline story. For traders, that leverage means moves in revenue, fuel, and sentiment can have an outsized impact on the stock.

Why Traders Are Watching AAL Right Now

AAL has thrown a lot at the tape in a short time, and traders are paying attention. At the Morgan Stanley Laguna Conference on 2026/09/16, American Airlines told the market it “feels really good” about hitting 16%-19% revenue growth in Q3 and labeled recent growth as “durable.” That word matters. It signals management thinks demand and pricing strength are not just a summer fluke.

The market liked what it heard. AAL jumped about 3% to $13.11 after the conference, a clean show of confidence from traders. For short-term setups, that kind of event-driven push often becomes the anchor low for future pullbacks. If AAL keeps holding above that post‑conference zone, bulls remain in control.

More premium seats usually mean higher yields per passenger, which can thicken margins even when fuel bites. Record enrollments in the AAdvantage loyalty program back that up — a bigger, stickier customer base can support both pricing and lucrative card partnerships.

The AAL story is not clean, and that’s exactly why active traders are circling it. Add in the STARLUX partnership, the Project Atlas sustainable fuel deal, and even industry tailwinds like the FAA’s AI-based Smart air-traffic tool, and American Airlines looks set up for higher-quality revenue over time.

On the other side, the cost reality bites. Barclays cut its AAL price target from $19 to $14 even while keeping an Overweight rating, and UBS trimmed EPS estimates on higher fuel. The balance sheet is still highly leveraged, and margins remain razor thin. For AAL, that means every move in jet fuel or macro sentiment hits hard.

title: Three-way race for FIDE Presidency reaches the finish line in Samarkand - EU Reporter
description:
The race to become the next president of the International Chess Federation (FIDE) is reaching its climax in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.
Better known as “Vishy”, Anand is a five-time world champion and one of the most respected figures in international chess.
Nevertheless, Turlov remains on Ukraine's sanctions list and does not enjoy the support of the Ukrainian Chess Federation.
More recently, he became a prominent figure in international chess through Freestyle Chess, the Chess960 venture he developed with Carlsen.
His campaign website is: https://wr2026.com/ Main picture: FIDE candidates Jan Henric Buettner and Timur Turlov Credit: Rafal Oleksiewicz/FIDE © FIDE Chess Olympiad 2026 Share this article:
text:
The race to become the next president of the International Chess Federation (FIDE) is reaching its climax in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Three candidates are vying for the top position, with voting taking place on 26 September. If no ticket secures the required majority in the first ballot, a second round will be held between the two leading candidates.

On Thursday (24 September), at a joint press conference, each candidate was invited to pitch for the top job. One candidate, Wadim Rosenstein, couldn't attend; no explanation was given. At an earlier online debate on 10 September, Rosenstein took part but left around ten minutes after the discussion began.

Runners and riders

Three tickets are in the race. Each is led by a high-profile entrepreneur, and all three candidates have emphasised how they intend to bring their business experience to the job.

Two of the contenders share a ticket with prominent figures from the chess world.

Jan Henric Buettner, a German serial entrepreneur, is running with British chess organiser Malcolm Pein for deputy president. Pein was involved in efforts that led to increased British government support for chess in 2023.

Freedom Holding founder and CEO Timur Turlov, who has headed the Kazakhstan Chess Federation since 2023, is running with legendary Indian grandmaster Viswanathan Anand. Better known as “Vishy”, Anand is a five-time world champion and one of the most respected figures in international chess.

The third contender is WR Chess founder and WR Group chairman Wadim Rosenstein, a German entrepreneur running alongside Gordon Tang of Singapore. Both have extensive business backgrounds, Rosenstein in logistics, infrastructure and real estate, and Tang in real estate.

Rosenstein's campaign has also hosted large social events alongside the election campaign, including an Aloha party and a Latin Caribbean Night.

Timur Turlov

In a short interview with EU Reporter, Turlov said one issue he heard most often from national delegations was the difficulty of accessing FIDE development funds.

“We definitely need better communication inside FIDE,” he said, arguing that application rules and criteria should be simplified.

Turlov said federations should have greater flexibility to decide how money is allocated between areas including open tournaments, travel and coaching for young players, and chess-in-schools initiatives.

Asked why federations should back his candidacy, Turlov pointed to his experience running Kazakhstan's chess federation, his business background and the resources available to his campaign.

“I have a team in place, resources in place, and a track record to do that,” he said.

Turlov also wants FIDE to broaden its corporate sponsorship base. He said he would approach international business partners and establish a professional commercial team within FIDE to attract sponsors, while stressing that the organisation could not focus solely on commercially attractive elite players.

“If we were a commercial organisation, we would monetise the top 10 players,” he said. “But we have to develop grassroots in chess.”

Addressing the political dimension of the FIDE election, Turlov described himself as a politically neutral candidate. In 2022, Turlov gained full Kazakh citizenship and renounced his Russian citizenship.

On Monday, 21 September, Turlov proposed Mykhailo Podolyak, adviser to the Office of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, for a role representing Ukraine within FIDE's leadership. Podolyak subsequently expressed support for Turlov's reform agenda.

Nevertheless, Turlov remains on Ukraine's sanctions list and does not enjoy the support of the Ukrainian Chess Federation.

He said FIDE should “follow international law”, respect decisions of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and comply with relevant regulations.

“For me, it’s easy to keep this position, to appreciate everyone,” Turlov said, adding that FIDE should respect the rules governing it “but at the same time not apply policy ourselves.”

Turlov's campaign website: https://turlovforchess.com/

Jan Henric Buettner

Buettner, co-founder of Freestyle Chess with former world champion Magnus Carlsen, is presenting himself as a non-political candidate seeking to reduce dependence on powerful patrons.

Speaking to EU Reporter, Buettner said his central message was greater independence for FIDE and its national federations.

“I’m definitely considering myself a non-political choice,” Buettner said, arguing that FIDE should move away from a system in which wealthy individuals promise financial support and federations become dependent on their patronage.

Instead, he said he wants to put FIDE “on its own legs”, strengthen its member federations and build a more commercially sustainable organisation. His campaign platform includes plans to generate new commercial revenue and distribute more resources across the chess ecosystem.

Buettner, 62, has a long career in technology, venture capital, property and hospitality. More recently, he became a prominent figure in international chess through Freestyle Chess, the Chess960 venture he developed with Carlsen.

Asked whether his election could encourage Carlsen to become more involved with FIDE events again, Buettner was cautious.

“Magnus always has his own head,” he said, adding that he had not discussed the election with him. Rather than trying to persuade Carlsen personally, Buettner said his aim would be to create a FIDE framework attractive enough for leading players “to voluntarily become a participant again.”

Buettner also sought to separate his FIDE ambitions from Freestyle Chess, stressing that traditional chess would remain at the federation's heart.

For Buettner, the attraction of the presidency is the scale of the challenge: bringing more than 200 national federations together while making FIDE less political.

“I think it’s a great challenge,” he said, “to get an organization that consists of 204 federations and nations into one unity and to do something really spectacular out of that.”

Buettner's website: https://janhenricbuettner.com/

EU Reporter did not get the opportunity to interview Wadim Rosenstein. His campaign website is: https://wr2026.com/

text:
Strategic Biofuels is building Louisiana Green Fuels (LGF), a carbon-negative waterfront facility in the Port of Columbia, Louisiana, that will produce low-carbon fuels and power. The Port of Columbia is highly supportive of LGF’s mission to produce sustainable aviation fuel and naphtha using forestry waste, mostly roundwood feedstock (logs and round sections of wood) from managed forests that is compliant with the federal renewable fuel standard. In addition, the site will feature a biomass power plant that will run primarily on sawmill waste and other usable biomass waste. The renewable fuels will be shipped by rail to California in compliance with that state’s Low Carbon Fuel Standard (LCFS). The project also features natural-gas and carbon-dioxide pipelines, three carbon capture utilization and storage (CCUS) injection wells, and utility interconnects.

As Owner’s Agent and Permitting and Regulatory Manager, Geosyntec’s primary responsibility is to de-risk the project through proactive and integrated permitting strategy and technical evaluations. This work includes oversight of environmental contractors carrying out cultural-resources and environmental field surveys. We developed a comprehensive permit matrix tool to track applicable authorizations, requirements to obtain approvals, time needed to develop the permit materials, agency review times, and critical issues to consider. The tool is also used to rank risks, manage permit fees and budgets, and identify any gaps as design progresses.

With the project in pre-FEED (pre-front-end engineering design), we built out the master schedule to include permitting and regulatory work that must be started or completed before construction begins. We also streamlined environmental surveys and reporting to align with United States Department of Energy (DOE) requirements. In addition to environmental services, we led the development of the community benefits plan, a key component of the overall DOE Title 17 Part II application.
